reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the speaker promotes the Forsage plan by claiming substantial earnings, directing viewers to enroll through a sponsor link for 18 BUSD or about 1,800 rupees, and describing slot purchases, recycling, team-building, and sponsorship as producing repeated or multiple returns. Although he says he once called the system a scam, he presents that as a rejected earlier view and continues the favorable pitch; his warning not to share wallet recovery words is separate from the enrollment and income claims. The displayed figures and claimed past earnings are not independently corroborated, and transaction outcomes are not established.

citations.quote: Do it now and apply the ID now.
According to the plan you will get the commission now.
And what did I say? This is a scam. It is a fraud.
But I didn't want to understand and I didn't want to listen to the other person.
If your upline is in working, it is working it is purchasing slot, it is making team, it is sponsoring people, only then you will get money.

opening.argument: Judge, the speaker does not present participation as risk-free. He says that buying a slot does not ensure earnings and explicitly warns viewers never to share their wallet recovery words. He also recounts initially suspecting fraud before explaining why he changed his mind. Those qualifications matter when assessing whether this is a deceptive solicitation: his earnings claims are forceful, but he also gives viewers information that cuts against an assumption of guaranteed returns or a request for wallet credentials.

I am requesting with a hand in hand, please don't share this 12 words with anyone you know. No way!
And what did I say? This is a scam. It is a fraud.
But I didn't want to understand and I didn't want to listen to the other person.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The immediate-action language and promised commission are real, but neither establishes that every entrant will receive a return. The same explanation allows for buying a slot without earning money. Nor does the speaker's earlier suspicion prove present fraud; he describes it as a view formed before he listened further. His recovery-word warning is separate from enrollment, but it is still relevant to whether he is trying to obtain viewers' credentials.

citations.quote: Whether you earn money or not
But I didn't want to understand and I didn't want to listen to the other person.
please don't share this 12 words with anyone you know. No way!

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The wallet warning addresses credential sharing, not the plan being promoted. The speaker tells viewers to apply an ID immediately, says they will receive commission according to the plan, and ties income to an upline purchasing slots, building a team, and sponsoring people. A brief acknowledgment that someone might not earn does not undo those recruitment-based income claims.

citations.quote: Do it now and apply the ID now. According to the plan you will get the commission now.
If your upline is in working, it is working it is purchasing slot, it is making team, it is sponsoring people, only then you will get money.

opening.argument: Judge, much of this presentation teaches viewers how to inspect and understand the system. The speaker describes opening an ID without a password, checking its statistics, and walking through the different matrix plans. That is more specific than a bare appeal to send money: he is showing the interface and explaining where payments are said to go. Treat the large figures as claims made during that demonstration, not as independently verified outcomes or, by themselves, proof of deception.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The enrollment instruction is a serious point, but it does not make the interface walkthrough fictitious or strip the detailed plan explanation of its instructional content. The prosecution also notes that claimed earnings are uncorroborated. That limits what the demonstration proves about actual returns; it does not establish that the speaker fabricated the interface or that every explanation of its mechanics is a fraudulent act.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The walkthrough serves an enrollment pitch. The speaker tells viewers to apply an ID now, specifies the amount needed to join, and directs them to use a sponsor's link. His matrix explanation then describes money reaching participants through people they connect and through the upline. Demonstrating an interface does not change the recruitment-based offer he is urging viewers to enter.

citations.quote: Do it now and apply the ID now.
you need to take the amount of 1800 rupees and as soon as you join the system, you have to run the link of an individual who will sponsor you
it is purchasing slot, it is making team, it is sponsoring people, only then you will get money.

opening.argument: Judge, the speaker describes a paid, sponsor-linked plan, but he also says income depends on people working; simply connecting is not enough. He expressly rejects the idea of buying a slot and doing nothing as advice to viewers. The cited account shows slot purchases and referrals, not an observed instance of someone being denied payment, losing access to a wallet, or having their recovery words collected. Without treating his earnings claims as verified, the narrower reading is a conditional referral promotion whose harmful outcome has not been demonstrated here.

citations.quote: You just connect and money will start coming. It won't come, friends.
If your upline is not in working, you will not get money in act 4.
But I will never give you a suggestion that you just buy a slot and go to sleep.
please don't share this 12 words with anyone you know. No way!

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution is right that slots, teams, and sponsors feature in the explanation. But those features alone do not document a blocked payment or a completed loss. The speaker even says that merely connecting does not start the money flowing and describes an upline's work as a condition. Those limits should carry weight before treating his conditional referral account as proof that viewers were defrauded.

citations.quote: You just connect and money will start coming. It won't come, friends.
If your upline is in working, it is working it is purchasing slot, it is making team, it is sponsoring people, only then you will get money.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A completed loss is not necessary to assess what the video promotes. The speaker instructs viewers to join with funds through an individual sponsor's link, says an upline makes money by purchasing slots, making a team, and sponsoring people, and tells viewers they can connect unlimited people. Calling those payments conditional does not turn the described recruitment-and-matrix income structure into an ordinary referral reward.
